background.executionContext:
**Commands used (in order):**
1. `./b4w.sh help` — discover available commands
2. `./b4w.sh goto "http://books.toscrape.com/"` — navigate
3. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot` — capture snapshot
4. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot inspect` — discover CSS selectors
5. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get text "article.product_pod h3 a"` — first try (truncated)
6. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get attr "article.product_pod h3 a" title` — full title via attr
7. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get html "article.product_pod"` — container HTML
8. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get attr "article.product_pod h3 a" href` — link href
9. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get all text "article.product_pod h3 a"` — all titles
10. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get all text "article.product_pod h3 a" --offset 5 --limit 5` — pagination
11. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot export --file .test-sessions/books-toscrape.html` — export (after discovering `--file` not `--output`)
12. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot summary` — page summary
13. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot grep "price" --all` — search for price
14. `grep -o "price" .test-sessions/books-toscrape.html | wc -l` — count occurrences

**Important decisions:**
- Used `./b4w.sh` instead of `./b4w.ps1` because the `.ps1` wrapper has CRLF line endings that break the shebang on Linux. The SKILL.md explicitly documents `./b4w.sh` as the correct wrapper for Linux/Git Bash/macOS.
- Used `htmlsnapshot inspect` to discover CSS selectors before extraction, as recommended by the documentation.
- Used `get attr ... title` to get full book titles after discovering `get text` returns CSS text-overflow truncated values.
- Used `grep -o | wc -l` on the exported file for accurate occurrence counting, since `htmlsnapshot grep` has no built-in count mode.

**Workarounds required:**
- CRLF fix: Used `./b4w.sh` instead of `./b4w.ps1` due to Windows line endings
- Truncated text: Used `title` attribute extraction as workaround for CSS text-overflow truncation in `get text`
- Export flag: Discovered `--file` is the correct flag (not `--output`) by running `--help`
- Count: Used shell pipe to `wc -l` since `htmlsnapshot grep` has no count feature

issues.title: b4w.ps1 has CRLF line endings — breaks shebang on Linux

sections.body: On Linux: `./b4w.ps1 help` → `/usr/bin/env: 'pwsh\r': No such file or directory`
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: b4w.ps1 should execute correctly on Linux if pwsh is available, or produce a clear error message explaining platform requirements.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The shebang `#!/usr/bin/env pwsh\r` includes a carriage return character from Windows CRLF line endings, causing the shell to look for a binary called `pwsh\r` which doesn't exist. The error message is confusing for users who have pwsh installed.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The b4w.ps1 file uses Windows-style CRLF line endings. On Linux, the kernel processes the shebang line literally, including the trailing \r as part of the interpreter name. The SKILL.md documents `./b4w.sh` as the Linux wrapper, but the error is cryptic and the `.ps1` file appears to be the primary entry point from the documentation.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1:1 — shebang line with CRLF line endings
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Convert b4w.ps1 to LF line endings (add a .gitattributes entry or run dos2unix)
- Add a pre-commit hook to enforce LF line endings on shell scripts
- Alternatively, add a shebang check at the top of b4w.sh that detects CRLF in b4w.ps1 and warns the user

issues.title: Text extraction shows CSS text-overflow truncated values instead of full text

sections.body: `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get text "article.product_pod h3 a"` → `A Light in the ...` (truncated) instead of `A Light in the Attic`
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Text extraction should return the full text content of the element, matching what `textContent` would return, or at minimum surface a hint that the extracted text is truncated.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The extracted text matches the visually rendered text (which includes CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis`), not the element's full `textContent`. Users must know to extract the `title` attribute instead.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The htmlsnapshot's text extraction appears to use the rendered/visible text rather than the DOM's `textContent`. This is likely by design for some use cases, but the truncation is not surfaced to the user — there's no hint that more text exists.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Surface a truncation hint when extracted text ends with '...' and suggest trying `get attr` to retrieve the full value from attributes like `title` or `alt`
- Consider offering a `--full-text` flag that uses `textContent` instead of visible text
- Add a tip in the output when truncated text is detected
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot export silently ignores unrecognized flags (--output vs --file)

sections.body: `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot export --output .test-sessions/books-toscrape.html` → saves to default path `.browser4-cli/snapshot/htmlsnapshot-....html` instead of the specified path, with no warning or error.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Unrecognized flags should produce an error (e.g., 'unknown option: --output') or at minimum a warning on stderr. Alternatively, `--output` should be added as an alias for `--file` since it's the conventional flag name users expect.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The `--output` flag was silently ignored. The export succeeded but saved to the default location, which could cause data loss if the user doesn't notice.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The CLI's argument parser does not reject unknown flags — it silently drops them. Combined with the fact that `--output` is the conventional GNU/POSIX flag for specifying an output file, users naturally reach for it.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — argument parsing logic that should reject unknown flags
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add `--output` as an alias for `--file` in the export command
- Reject unknown flags with a clear error message rather than silently ignoring them
- Add a convention note in the help output explaining that `--file` is used for output paths
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot grep lacks built-in count mode

sections.body: `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot grep "price"` shows matching lines but provides no count summary. Users must pipe to external tools (grep -c, wc -l) to count occurrences.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A grep tool should offer a `--count`/`-c` flag that outputs the number of matching lines or occurrences, similar to standard `grep -c`.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: No count flag exists. The output is paginated by default, requiring `--all` to disable pagination, then shell piping to count. The pagination footer says 'showing 20 of 64 matches' which provides a line count but no occurrence count within lines.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The htmlsnapshot grep feature was designed for content search/display, not for counting. The line count in the pagination footer is the closest built-in feature.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add `--count`/`-c` flag to htmlsnapshot grep that outputs just the count
- Add `--count-matches` flag that counts all occurrences (not just matching lines)
- Include match count in the pagination footer even when `--all` is used
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No auto-discovery hint when text extraction returns truncated values

sections.body: Run `htmlsnapshot get text` on any element where CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis` is applied. The truncated output looks like the full value to a new user.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: When text extraction returns content ending with '...', the CLI should surface a tip suggesting the user try `get attr` to retrieve the `title` attribute (which often contains the full text), or show a truncation indicator.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: No hint is provided. A new user would assume 'A Light in the ...' is the actual title text.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The htmlsnapshot text extraction doesn't differentiate between actual text ending in '...' (like a deliberate ellipsis in a title) and CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis` truncation. The system doesn't know it's truncated.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- In the HTML snapshot capture phase, detect elements where `offsetWidth < scrollWidth` (CSS text-overflow) and flag them
- When `get text` returns content ending with '...' for a flagged element, add a stderr tip: 'This element's visible text is CSS-truncated. Try `get attr ... title` for the full text.'
- The inspect output already shows truncated text; add a visual indicator (e.g., '…' vs '...' for deliberate ellipsis)
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot grep default pagination requires --all for complete results

sections.body: `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot grep "price"` shows only 20 of 64 matches and requires the user to know about `--all` to get the full result set.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The pagination should either be documented more prominently in the grep help, or `--all` should be the default for grep (since grep is typically used for searching, not browsing).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Default pagination at 20 matches requires extra flag to disable. The pagination footer mentions `--all` but a new user might miss it.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Grep inherits the same pagination default as `get html` commands, but grep's primary use case (searching) differs from browsing HTML output.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Consider making `--all` the default for `htmlsnapshot grep` since the primary use case is searching
- Alternatively, print the pagination footer more prominently when results are truncated
- Add a tip: 'Use --all to see all matches' in the output
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
